terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: northern Thai cloth temple lantern with gilt collars, vertical ribs and a pleated skirt
motionPotential: swings on its hanger as a whole rigid body - nothing articulates
objectClass.notes: The northern Thai temple lantern hung in ranks along temple eaves and through Chiang Mai during Yi Peng. Radially symmetric, so the single view shows the whole form.

reasoning: One lathed body carrying the barrel, both gilt collars and the pleated skirt, plus ONE InstancedMesh for the twelve vertical ribs - two draw calls, the entire medium ceiling.

The ribs earn the second draw call here in a way the Chinese lantern's did not: on this lantern they are gilt against cream and run the full height, so they are the feature that separates a Lanna lantern from a plain cloth drum.
The gilt collars are a COLOUR change on the cloth surface, so they are vertex-colour bands rather than a third material.
It hangs, so the pivot is at top-center and the whole prop occupies negative Y.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate. The medium class allows only TWO draw calls and TWO materials, so all sub-structure is carried as lathe profile detail, vertex-colour regions and localFeatures.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Twenty ribs running the drum's full height.
A stiff twenty-pleat fan flaring below the drum and turning back up at its hem.
A nearly straight drum easing in at both ends, not a plump barrel.
The skirt meeting the drum's foot band with no daylight between them.
A domed gilt cap over the drum's head.
Three gilt bands at the drum head, drum foot and skirt shoulder.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: Radially symmetric, so nothing is hidden by the single view. Confidence 0.95.
Rib count is read off the plate as twelve; at 0.42 m the exact count is not identity-critical. Confidence 0.65.
The skirt's scalloped hem is authored as a smooth flare: a scallop needs either a much denser lathe or a second repetition system, and the medium class has neither to spare. Confidence 0.8.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: All intake unknowns are RESOLVED; each has a chosen answer and a stated confidence in resolvedUnknowns and in spec.assumptions. Nothing here blocks implementation, and the ones a second view would settle are not resolvable from a single plate by any amount of further analysis.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: bbox against 0.42 x 0.72 x 0.42 m and hanging entirely below y=0
the skirt re-flares below the lower collar
twelve ribs readable and seated on the cloth
turntable hole gate at all four azimuths
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure is measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not taper the profile monotonically to the hem; the skirt must flare back out.
Do not author a third material for the collars; they are a colour region on the cloth.
Do not put a sharp corner in the lathe profile - a shared disc/wall vertex shades as a dark ring the gate reads as a hole.
Do not add a second pivot or any socket.
qualityContract.depthRationale: TWO components across two material layers. Six micro-feature groups: the drum profile, its vertical ribs, the skirt flare, the skirt junction, the gold cap and the three gathering bands.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.criteria: Measured bbox must be 0.42 x 0.72 x 0.42 m within tolerance, hanging entirely below y=0.

featureReviewTargets.name: Pleated skirt
featureReviewTargets.criteria: The skirt must be a STIFF PLEATED FAN that flares and folds back at the hem, hanging directly off the drum's foot band. A smooth bag or a plain cone fails -- the asset notes make the scalloped skirt the thing that distinguishes this lantern from the round red Chinese one.

featureReviewTargets.name: Gilt vertical ribs
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Ribs must run the drum's full height as geometry around the axis, not as separate sticks beside it.

featureReviewTargets.name: Material response
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Cream cloth against gilt trim, with the cloth near the measured 185-202 and comfortably clear of the ~58 backdrop.

lookDevTargets.keyLightIntent: Hemisphere light plus three directionals, ACES tone mapping, no environment map.
lookDevTargets.materialSeparation: cream cloth 185-202 / gilt trim and skirt 139-163 in measured plate luma.
lookDevTargets.holeGateFloor: No surface may render at or near the ~58 backdrop luma at any turntable azimuth, including the back-lit 180 frame which renders at ~0.55 of painted luma.
lookDevTargets.notes: Metalness is held below 1.0 on every metal because there is no environment map to reflect.

actionReadiness.notes: Explodable and clickable as two named parts. Not articulated and not breakable.

assumptions: Radially symmetric, so nothing is hidden by the single view.
Rib count is twelve, read off the plate; at 0.42 m the exact count is not identity-critical.
The scalloped hem is authored as a smooth flare - a scallop needs a much denser lathe or a second repetition system, and the medium class has neither to spare.
The lantern is a rigid body: it swings on its hanger as a whole and nothing articulates.

coordinateFrame.originPolicy: top-center: the origin sits at the hanging point on the lantern's axis, and the whole prop occupies negative Y so it hangs from a ceiling with no offset.

silhouette.derivation: Measured bbox 0.441 x 0.721 x 0.441 m against the declared 0.42 x 0.72 x 0.42 -- exact on height, 5% over on width and depth, the overshoot being the skirt's pleat crests standing proud of the drum's r 0.21.
silhouette.symmetry: radial about the Y axis, broken only by the twelve ribs, which are themselves radially periodic
silhouette.notes: Radially symmetric, so the single plate shows the whole form.

componentTree.name: Ribbed cream drum and its scalloped skirt
componentTree.topologyRationale: TWO ribbedDomes on one material and one submission -- the drum and the skirt. A ribbedDome modulates a profile AROUND its axis, so twenty ribs up the drum and twenty pleats round the skirt are two surfaces of revolution rather than forty authored folds, which is the whole reason this prop is cheap. A lathe is constant around its own axis and can carry neither.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Origin TOP-CENTER at the hanging point, which is the crown of the hanging rope's loop, so the prop occupies y -1.02 to 0 and the fixture itself y -1.02 to -0.30. A 60-segment drum over a nearly straight profile easing in at both ends, r 0.088 to 0.21, between y -0.44 and -0.06; and a 60-segment skirt from the drum's foot band at -0.470 flaring to r 0.214 and turning back up at its hem at -0.716.

localFeatures.description: Twenty ribs running the drum's full height at 10 mm amplitude, tinted toward a darker cream at the troughs. The previous build had a plain cylinder with a few loose gold sticks beside it.

A stiff pleated fan, not a bag: twenty pleats at 30 mm amplitude over a profile that flares to r 0.214 and then TURNS BACK UP at the hem, which is what gives the folded lip the plate shows. The previous build hung a smooth ellipsoid there.

A nearly straight drum easing in at both ends where the cloth is gathered into its bands, which is what distinguishes this lantern from the plump red Chinese barrel -- the difference the asset notes make its identity.

The skirt reaches UP to the drum's foot band at -0.470. Ending it lower left a 75 mm gap you could see straight through; the plate's skirt hangs directly off the foot band with no daylight between them.

componentTree.notes: Cream #d8cfb4 with rib troughs #bfae7e as a vertex colour. Luma 186, far above the mask's erased window, so no tone correction was needed.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Cream cloth carrying its rib and pleat troughs as a vertex colour.

componentTree.name: Gold cap, rope eyelet and the drum bands
componentTree.topologyRationale: Gilt against cream cloth is the prop's only colour contrast, and cap, bands and eyelet are one material and therefore one submission.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A domed gold cap, bands at the drum's head and foot, a band at the skirt's shoulder, and a gold eyelet on the cap the hanging cord rises from. The whole fixture sits 0.30 m below the origin now: the origin is the crown of the rope's loop.

localFeatures.description: A domed gold cap over the drum's head, at the top-center pivot.
Three gold bands -- drum head, drum foot and skirt shoulder -- each where the cloth is gathered. They are what make the drum and skirt read as one lantern rather than two stacked shapes.

componentTree.name: Jute hanging cord with its loop
componentTree.topologyRationale: Owner addition (2026-09-03): a cord the lantern can hang from. Its own material because jute is neither gilt nor cloth, and a rope tile needs a material of its own to bind to; one cylinder, one collar and one swept loop in one submission.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 14 mm cord rising from the cap's eyelet (y -0.31) through a whipped knot at y -0.066 to a loop of r 0.023 swept in the XY plane whose crown is y 0 -- the hanging point and the origin. 0.30 m of rope, so the declared height is 1.02.

attachment.notes: The cord's foot is buried in the gold eyelet on the cap.

localFeatures.description: A swept loop at the top of the cord, crown at the origin, closed on a whipped knot.
Laid-strand relief from a rope tile on culm UVs, running along the cord and round the loop.

componentTree.notes: Rope #b09f7c on a white vertexColors material.

repetitionSystems.name: Vertical gilt ribs
repetitionSystems.rationale: Twelve ribs as ONE InstancedMesh - the second and last draw call this prop has. Two numbers here are measured against the barrel rather than chosen: the ribs are 0.180 m tall, not the 0.340 m of the full barrel, and they sit at 0.206 m from the axis. Authored 0.340 m tall at 0.202 m they ran past the barrel's shoulders, where the profile has narrowed to r 0.158, and rendered as twelve slats floating clear of the cloth. Confined to y -0.38..-0.20, where the profile holds r 0.200-0.210, each rib now stands about 6 mm proud of the surface - a raised rib, which is what the plate shows.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.441 x 0.721 x 0.441 m against the declared 0.42 x 0.72 x 0.42 -- exact on height, 5% over on width and depth, the overshoot being the skirt's pleat crests standing proud of the drum's r 0.21. Against the plate the drum is a little squatter and the skirt a little wider than ideal, which is the honest residual.

A stiff twenty-pleat fan at 30 mm amplitude over a profile that flares to r 0.214 and TURNS BACK UP at the hem, which is what gives the folded lip the plate shows. The previous build hung a smooth ellipsoid there. It also had to reach up to the drum's foot band: at its first position a 75 mm gap opened between drum and skirt that you could see straight through, where the plate's skirt hangs directly off the band.

Twenty ribs running the drum's full height as a modulation around the axis, tinted toward a darker cream at the troughs. A lathe is constant around its own axis and cannot carry them, which is why both drum and skirt are ribbedDomes -- forty folds for two submissions. The previous build had a plain cylinder with a few loose gold sticks standing beside it.

Two material layers: cream cloth at luma 186 carrying its rib troughs as a vertex colour, and gilt trim at luma 150 for the cap, the three gathering bands and the hanging wire. Both sit far above gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window, so unlike this kit's dark props neither needed a tone correction. Roughness 0.90 on the cloth -- matt, with no specular band that could rise into the window. NOT carried: the plate's gold rib TAPES, which are applied strips over the cloth rather than the tinted troughs used here.

The 4 mm gold wire stub the plate showed is replaced by the cord the owner asked for; it rises from a gold eyelet on the cap through a whipped knot to a loop of r 0.023 whose crown is the origin.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A mid-grey backdrop at luma ~114 - DARKER than the lantern, which is the opposite of most plates in this kit; foreground coverage is 41.8%. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why every metal here is authored below metalness 1.0: a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, and it renders DARKER than the 58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

The review harness applies ACES filmic tone mapping, which rolls off highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value. Albedo is therefore verified in the render and corrected against the measurement rather than copied through from the crop.

Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken joints and seams. The prop's ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.
